title: Serving runtime weekly update — kernel/KV/batching (2026-06-10)
content:
Summary:
Quick weekly sync from serving-runtime focused on kernel fusion, KV cache correctness and eviction, and dynamic batching improvements. Overall progress is good: kernel refactor PRs are mostly green on CI, KV cache fixes resolved a correctness edge-case for long-prefix reuse, and batching experiments reduced p95 on small sequences. Still working on a memory regression introduced by kernel tiling on A100 and a flaky integration test for multi-tenant cache isolation.

Highlights:
- Kernel refactor PR #4623 merged to main branch — removes legacy queue-managed tiling path and consolidates tiled matmul code paths. Expect ~5-8% token throughput improvement on transformer-deep models at 2k seq.
- KV cache bugfix (SERVR-1284) deployed to canary; fixes an incorrect cache index computation that caused stale KV reads for sequence lengths > 4096 when using prefix caching + rotate pruning. Canary traffic shows no regressions so far.
- Dynamic batching pilot decreased p95 for short-chat workloads (avg seq length ~64) from 240ms -> 210ms on p95 under medium load. Improvements came primarily from smarter microbatch packing heuristic and lowering per-request scheduling jitter.

Kernel work (Aisha / Miguel):
- Merged PR 4623: major refactor of tiled GEMM path. Code simplified, kernel selection logic centralized.
- Microbenchmark numbers (internal): bert-large-like model, A100-80GB, batch size 1 latency: p50 -2%, p95 -4%; throughput +6% at steady-state.
- Outstanding: memory regression seen on some A100 nodes during extended runs (12h). Hypothesis: temporary buffer alignment change caused additional pinned memory allocations. Action: revert alignment tweak in branch and run long-job stress tests. (Owner: Miguel)
- Next: Add fallback path for small-matmul fastpath when sequence < 32 to avoid overhead on tiny sequences.

KV cache (Priya / Samir):
- Deployed fix for stale-index bug in canary cluster (SERVR-1284). Root cause: off-by-one when shifting cache index during prefix rotation under heavy prefix reuse.
- Canary metrics: cache hit rate stable; no increase in stale response errors. End-to-end tests added to catch rotation-edgecases.
- Multi-tenant isolation flaky test (SERVR-1302): occasionally cross-tenant cache leak detected in simulated multi-tenant scenario. Repro steps added to a new integration test. Investigation points to a race in eviction + background compaction.
- Plan: implement a short-term mutex around compaction + eviction and a longer-term lock-free compaction strategy. (Owner: Priya)

Batching (Leah / Connor):
- Dynamic batcher pilot in prod-sim reduced p95 for short sequences. Key changes: packing timeout reduced from 4ms -> 2ms, improved packer that groups by token-length buckets.
- Observed a side-effect: slight increase in p50 variability under bursty traffic patterns due to tighter timeout combined with OS scheduling. Mitigation: adaptive timeout — increase timeout by 1ms when burstiness detected. Experiment scheduled next week.
- Microbatch accounting: introduced per-request metadata for batch lineage to help trace high-latency outliers. This will feed into Console heatmaps.

Metrics & Observability (Connor):
- Current numbers (canary cluster, last 24h): p50=28ms, p95=210ms, 99=380ms for short-chat workload. Token throughput: +5% vs prior week.
- New dashboards: kernel-kpi, kv-cache-hit-rate, batch-packing-latency. Link to dashboards in linked artifacts.

Blockers / Risks:
- Memory regression on A100 nodes could affect Dedicated customers running long steady-state workloads. Critical to resolve before next Dedicated release.
- Multi-tenant KV leak still unrepro'd outside integration test; risk for Private deployments where tenant isolation guaranteed by policy.
- One flaky e2e test in CI (test/multi-tenant/cache_isolation_test) causing occasional pipeline failures — tracked as SERVR-1302.

Action items / Next week:
- Miguel: bisect to find exact commit introducing A100 memory regression; revert alignment change if needed and run 24h stress test (ETA: 2026-06-14).
- Priya: implement short-term eviction mutex in KV compaction and add stronger invariants in unit tests (ETA: 2026-06-12).
- Leah & Connor: run adaptive batching experiment in canary, monitor p95 and p50 variability (start: 2026-06-11).
- Aisha: add small-sequence fastpath in kernel selection (RFC by 2026-06-15).
- Team: add end-to-end scenario to perf lab for 48h soak with canary kernel + new KV compaction to catch regressions early (coordinators: Miguel / Priya).

Notes / Misc:
- We should sync with SRE on Dedicated fleet scheduling to understand swap pressure observed during prolonged runs. Meeting requested (SRE sync) for 2026-06-12.
- Suggestion from support: provide temporary knob to disable tiled path per-deployment in case of emergency rollback without full binary revert. File an RFC if we want to pursue.

Meeting log (2026-06-10 standup):
- Quick round: Miguel noted the A100 issue; Priya confirmed canary passed KV fix; Leah reported batching pilot metrics; Connor summarized dashboard additions.
- Decisions: merge PR 4623 (done), deploy KV fix to canary (done), run adaptive batching experiment (approved).

If anything urgent, ping #serving-runtime on Slack. Will follow up next week with updated perf numbers and canary feedback.

-- Connor
